newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens networks turnover to rise in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Siemens networks turnover to rise in 96/97.

text.p: Siemens' public telecommunications networks group said on Friday it would raise turnover in the 1996/97 business year to 12.8 billion marks ($8.2 billion) from 11.8 billion marks in the year to this September 30.
Peter Pribilla, head of the networks group and a member of parent Siemens AG's board, told that growth would be driven by fast-growing markets in Asia and eastern Europe.
Pribilla told reporters that, while the Asian market was expected to grow by eight percent a year, Siemens wanted to boost its network sales by 12 percent annually.
Meanwhile, in eastern Europe, business is planned to grow by an annual 11 percent -- compared to market expansion range of between seven and 12 percent, he said.
The share of foreign business should rise from two-thirds now to 80 percent over the next three years, he added.
In the business year just ended, Siemens public networks made a pre-tax profit up over 70 percent to 354 million marks.
